headline: Single-cell profiling maps human tissue states and regulatory programs in disease
label: Single Cell Atlases Regulatory Inference
summary: Integrated single-cell atlases and new profiling and modeling methods now link cell states to regulatory programs across human tissues.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell resolution of cell-state composition and the regulatory logic behind it. An integrated kidney atlas harmonizes 18 scRNA/snRNA-seq datasets from 232 donors into 63 cell types and 120 cell states, while a pancreas multi-omic atlas addresses plasticity across development, health, and disease, and a glomerular disease snRNA-seq atlas identifies disease-associated states. Methodological advances extend this scope: OneCell CUT&Tag measures chromatin, transcriptome, and surface markers simultaneously in rare populations; a telegraph-model framework infers transcriptional burst frequency and size genome-wide; scDECIPHER infers logical regulatory models of cell state transitions; and ArchetypeShift adds KEGG and IPA annotation to scRNA-seq archetypes. Other items, including a 16-tissue Pareto archetype analysis, a single-cell eQTL commentary on esophageal squamous cell carcinoma risk, and a spatial cell-cell communication review, extend the theme to cross-tissue and spatial contexts.
